haiku-low.q1: Reads reports.row_count from the replica. At 10,000 or fewer, it builds the CSV in memory and returns it as a download. Above 10,000, it returns 202 and a status panel, then emails a link.
haiku-low.q2: The click returns the existing queued or running export with 202 and the status panel, after stale checks. No new export or job is created, regardless of filters.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation; no cleanup job is built. Download endpoint returns 410 after that.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, each with a 30-minute limit. After the third failure, the row is marked failed with a short reason, and a failure email is sent. The page shows the reason and a button to export again.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica, never the primary. Export state is stored on the primary.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary. The page calls the latest endpoint on load and polls every 5 seconds while queued or running, so reopening it shows current state.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica, formats them into an 8 MB in-memory buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part. The whole report is never held in memory.
haiku-low.q8: After an exception, abort_multipart is called and the attempt retries. After a timeout or dead worker, the incomplete upload is discarded by the lifecycle rule within 24 hours. Nothing is visible at the key. Each attempt restarts from the beginning, since the queue keeps no progress.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and cols are stored on the report_exports row, normalised from the URL. The job loads the row from the primary and reads them from there; the payload holds only export_id.
haiku-low.q10: A unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The second insert fails, and that request returns the first request's row without queuing a second job.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be fully uploaded and completed, status set to done with object_key stored, before the email. If a rerun finds done without email_sent_at, it only sends the email. If done with email sent, or failed, it stops.
haiku-low.q12: A replica error during the scan returns 503 with no body. The browser never saves a truncated file, and the user clicks again. Nothing is stored.

sonnet.q1: Step 1 reads reports.row_count from the replica. At 10,000 rows or fewer it takes the sync path: the whole CSV is built in memory and returned directly as 200 text/csv with Content-Disposition attachment. Above 10,000 it takes the large path: a report_exports row is created, a background job is queued, and the user gets 202 with the export id and status, then a status panel. Later the user gets an email with a link and a Download button on the page. If the sync scan reaches row 10,001 (stale count), it discards the buffer and goes to the large path with a 202.
sonnet.q2: Step 3 of the click finds the user's active (queued or running) export for that report before the size check. It runs the stale checks, then returns that existing export with 202 and the status panel. No new row or job is created, even if the filters differ. A queued row with no job_id older than 10 min is re-enqueued. A running row with updated_at older than 2 hours is marked failed and the new click goes ahead.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link is a signed URL created when the email is sent and works for 24 hours. The exports bucket lifecycle rule deletes each object 7 days after creation (it also discards incomplete multipart uploads after 24 hours). No cleanup job is built.
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts, with 60 s before attempt 2 and 300 s before attempt 3. After the third failure on_final_failure runs once. It aborts any upload, sets status failed with a short error reason, and sends the 'export_failed' email (report_name, export_id). The page shows the failed status with the reason and a button to start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica. Report rows are read only from it, never the primary. This applies to the sync path and the job (which uses the shared query code). The primary holds export state.
sonnet.q6: On the report_exports row on the primary, so a new state is seen at once. On load, the page calls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest, which reads from the primary. If the status is queued or running it shows a status panel and polls every 5 s until done or failed, stopping when the page is hidden or left. A reopened page learns the state from that load call. done shows a Download button, failed shows the reason, and a done export over 7 days old shows 'expired'.
sonnet.q7: It streams the file to storage as a multipart upload. It reads 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica, formats them as CSV into an in-memory buffer, and uploads each 8 MB buffer as a part, keeping the etag and clearing the buffer. It uploads the last buffer, then completes the upload. Peak memory is about one 8 MB buffer plus one page of rows, so the whole report is never held in memory. The plan sets a measurement gate on the 2M-row report on a real 512 MB worker: under 900 s and under 256 MB peak memory. If time fails, tune page and part size, then add checkpoints.
sonnet.q8: The next attempt starts from the beginning, because the queue keeps no progress and checkpoints are built only if the measurement gate fails. On an exception, abort_multipart discards the parts and the job re-raises. On a timeout or dead worker no code runs, so the incomplete upload is discarded by the lifecycle rule after 24 hours. The next attempt starts a new upload and overwrites upload_id. Nothing is visible at the key until the upload completes, so a half-written file can never be downloaded.
sonnet.q9: They are sent in the POST body, taken from the page URL, then validated and normalised and stored as the filters and cols columns on the report_exports row on the primary. The job payload is only {export_id}, and the job loads the row to get them.
sonnet.q10: A unique partial index on report_exports (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running'). The second insert fails. That request then reads and returns the row the first request created, and no second job is queued.
sonnet.q11: The file must be fully uploaded and the multipart upload completed, then the row set to done with object_key, completed_at and upload_id null. The email is sent after that and email_sent_at is then set. On a rerun the job loads the row. If it is done and the email was not sent, it skips straight to sending the email. If it is done with the email sent, or failed, it stops, so there is no second email.
sonnet.q12: A replica error during the sync scan returns 503 with no body. Nothing has been sent, because the full CSV is held until the scan finishes, so the browser never saves a truncated file. Nothing is stored, and the user just clicks again.
